overview: The easiest possible way to get computer vision working in a hobbyist project: plug a standard UVC-class (USB Video Class) webcam into any computer with a USB port — a laptop, a Raspberry Pi, a Jetson Nano — and libraries like OpenCV can open it with a couple of lines of code, no driver installation or protocol wrangling required. The tradeoff versus a dedicated camera module (Pi Camera, ESP32-CAM) is that it needs a real USB host with enough processing power to run the vision software; it's not something a bare Arduino or other microcontroller-class board can use directly.
simpleSummary: A plug-and-play camera for adding computer vision to any project with a USB port.

specifications.interface: USB (UVC class — works without custom drivers on Linux/Windows/macOS)
specifications.powerSource: Powered entirely through the USB connection, no separate power needed

pinMap.name: USB Connector
pinMap.function: Single USB connection carrying both power and video data using the standard UVC protocol.
pinMap.gotcha: Requires a real computer (Pi, Jetson, laptop) to run the host-side software — it cannot be read directly by a bare microcontroller like an Arduino or ESP32.
